Timeline::second¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::second() const

second() is the sole public spelling.

Read The Whole-Second Component¶

second() extracts the whole-second field in the range 0 through 59. It does not include the fractional portion: a timestamp ending in 08.009010011 returns 8, while nanosecond() returns the fraction.

The output is a shape-preserving int32 Series. NaT produces -1.

Example: Whole And Fractional Parts Stay Separate¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2020-12-31T23:59:59.123456789Z",
    "2021-01-01T00:00:00.987654321Z",
    "2024-02-29T06:07:08.009010011Z",
    "",
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, events.second());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[59, 0, 8, -1]

To reconstruct the within-minute numeric offset at nanosecond precision, pair the field with nanosecond(): conceptually second * 1'000'000'000 + nanosecond. Guard NaT first, because both absent sentinels are -1 and are not valid temporal components.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • second() truncates nothing itself; it selects the already stored whole second and leaves the subsecond field to the precision extractors.

  • It is not epoch seconds. Use an epoch export when absolute numeric time is required.

  • Equal second fields do not imply equal timestamps.
